set.body:
COUNTER-EVIDENCE BEAD, and the strongest one in this workstream. I had recorded that I could not vouch for the block claim in README:7-13 and DESCRIPTION:9 - that spatial node effects and cross-node coupling are the diagonal and off-diagonal blocks of ONE evidence operator. I tested it. It is literally true.

TEST 1 - BLOCKS DECOMPOSE EXACTLY. If node effects and coupling are genuinely blocks of one operator, computing a sub-block alone must equal extracting it from the whole. Built a 4-edge measurement_form over two rank-one nodes, then rebuilt each block in isolation:

  diagonal  anterior->anterior    in full 1.49991071428571   alone 1.49991071428571   diff 0
  offdiag   posterior->anterior   in full 1.24258928571429   alone 1.24258928571429   diff 0

Bitwise identical, not merely close. The operator decomposes.

TEST 2 - THE DIAGONAL BLOCK IS THE NODE'S OWN EFFECT. Hand-computed the within-node variation directly from the session matrices under the same centering operator:

  hand-computed  1.49991071428571
  package block  1.49991071428571
  abs diff       2.22e-16   (machine epsilon)

TEST 3 - THE OFF-DIAGONAL IS CROSS-NODE COVARIATION. Hand-computed the cross term:

  hand-computed  -1.24258928571429
  package block   1.24258928571429   (frobenius_strength is a norm, so magnitude)

and connectivity(view = 'correlation') returns -0.9912024, so the sign is preserved and reachable through the appropriate view rather than lost.

The block_index confirms the storage matches the claim structurally as well: four blocks with offset_elements and length_elements into one flat store, with left_axis and right_axis identity hashes per block.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND BEING TRUE. The unification is now verified on BOTH sides of the package:

  self-geometry core   a fixed neural metric composes into plan_geometry and returns the SAME
                       effect_geometry class, with rdm() values scaling exactly as the metric
                       dictates (K = 2I gives exactly 2x). contrast, rdm, rsa and spectrum are
                       all queries against that one object.
  measurement side     diagonal blocks are node effects, off-diagonal blocks are coupling, and
                       the blocks decompose exactly.

So the claim in README:7-13 is not marketing. It is an accurate description of what the code does, and it survives hand-computation on both halves.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE API WORK, and this is why the bead is filed rather than just noted. Since coupling really is the same operator, the API fragmentation is even less justified than the earlier beads argued. The measurement side currently has its own parallel constructor vocabulary - measurement_frame separate from compile_frame, edge_frame separate from pairing, measurement_form separate from geometry - for what is provably one object. The same 'one noun, three knobs' treatment proposed on bd-01KZYAV8X93BX4VC13Z8PK8XRH should extend here, with node pairs entering as a frame rather than as a separate object family.

The package's central intellectual claim is true and its API is the main thing preventing anyone from seeing that.
set.title: Verified by hand-computation: the unification claim holds on both sides of the framework
